name: Phaea
body:
Phaea
CR 7/MR 2

This titanic swine’s tough, hairy hide is stretched taut over rippling muscles, with bloodshot eyes under beetling brows and sharp, blood-stained tusks.

XP 3,200
N Huge animal (mythic)
Init -1; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 7, flat-footed 18 (-1 Dex, +11 natural, –2 size)
hp 85 (6d8+58)
Fort +10, Ref +4, Will +5
Defensive Abilities ferocity; DR 5/epic; Immune charm, fear

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee gore +13 (2d8+16 plus 1d4 bleed)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks ferocity, mythic power (2/day, surge +1d6), razor tusks, tramplema (2d6+16, DC 24)

STATISTICS

Str 33, Dex 8, Con 21, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 12
Base Atk +4; CMB +17; CMD 26 (30 vs. trip)
Feats Intimidating Prowess, Iron Will, ToughnessMF
Skills Intimidate +16 (+20 vs. Large or smaller foes), Perception +8
SQ foul-tempered

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Foul-Tempered (Ex)

A phaea is immune to charm and fear effects.

Intimidate is a class skill for a phaea, and when it hits with a melee attack it can make an Intimidate check against the target as a move action, or as a free action if it hits a target as part of a charge.

In addition, if a mythic boar is brought below 0 hp, it gains a +4 morale bonus on its Fortitude and Will saves and a +2 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls.

Razor Tusks (Ex)

A phaea’s gore attack inflicts 1d4 points of bleed damage. This bleed damage stacks. When it confirms a critical hit with its gore, it doubles the amount of bleed damage, and the Heal check DC increases to 17 to stop the bleeding.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate or tropical forests
Organization solitary, pair, or herd (1 phaea and 3–8 dire boars)
Treasure none

These enormous swine are savage man-eaters, with fur and hide ranging from brownish-black to tawny or even golden.

Their tusks are deadly sharp and they are extremely aggressive, prone to charge at any creature that crosses their path big enough to seem like a worthy meal. They can subsist on plant matter but prefer the taste of flesh. These beasts may be known by the lands where hey are found, such as the Calydonian Boar, Erymanthian Boar, or Krommyonian Sow and their first progenitors were unleashed upon mortal kingdoms in vengeance by the gods for slights against them.
